thread:
Sasha: heads-up — ops and runtime want a small set of new stability metrics plumbed into the infra dashboards: route_p95_latency, route_error_rate, inflight_queue_length, and exporter_failures. need to coordinate exporters + agg jobs + retention/backfill.
Maya: ok — which exporters are in scope? runtime HTTP + routing + queue exporter?
Sasha: correct. runtime-http-exporter, router-exporter, and the new queue-exporter (lightweight) that Oli prototyped. keep it minimal at first.
Liam: on the agg side we need to decide aggregation windows. p95 should be 1m/5m/1h rollups; error_rate at 1m/5m; inflight_count as gauge with 10s scrape but rollups at 1m. coarse 1h rollups for long-term.
Jonathan: for dashboard UX I want per-route selector and an overall cluster view. also a small panel that shows routing policy version and canary status.
Oliver: backfill note — the router only started exporting route identifiers consistently after 2025-01-10. backfill will require label normalization and deduping.
Maya: I'll open a PR to add route_p95 and error_rate to runtime-http-exporter. plan to keep label set small: {service, route, region, release_channel}. no user IDs.
Sasha: good. for retention: high-card metrics (route-level p95) -> 90d default, cluster-level aggregates -> 365d. we want to avoid exploding storage.
Liam: agree. aggregation job changes: add 1m->5m downsampling and new 1h rollup pipeline. I'll need a schema change for the aggregator output metric names.
Maya: example exporter snippet I plan to add:
```
metrics.register_histogram('route_latency_seconds', labels=['service','route','region','release_channel'])
# expose p95 via summaries on the ingestion side
```
Liam: for aggregation rename proposal: `route_latency_p95_1m`, `route_latency_p95_5m`, `route_latency_p95_1h`. keeps dashboards simple.
Jonathan: dashboard layout preference: top row cluster p95 + error rate sparkline, second row route selector + breakdown, third row alerts summary. will mock tomorrow.
Oliver: backfill plan sketch:
- run normalization job to map old route keys -> canonical routes
- run backfill window 2025-01-10 -> 2025-03-01
- inject into aggregator test namespace first
command prototype:
```
python tools/backfill_metrics.py --metric route_latency_p95 --start 2025-01-10 --end 2025-03-01 --normalize-routes
```
Oliver: estimate: 4-6 hours of cluster time, may spike ingest. schedule during low traffic.
Sasha: risk mitigation: canary backfill into `ingest-test` then sweep to prod. also set a temporary quota for the backfill job and monitor queue depth.
Maya: PR will include a feature flag `enable_route_labels` that default off. will add a migration note.
Liam: aggregator change will be behind a rollout flag too. we can route 5% of traffic to new aggregator outputs for 48h then increase.
Jonathan: + add a small rollout UX knob in the Console -> Telemetry -> Feature flags so SRE can flip. relevant for canarying both exporter labels & aggregator outputs.
Sasha: who owns what? Maya -> exporter PR + migration notes. Liam -> aggregation job + rollout. Jonathan -> dashboard mock + panels. Oliver -> backfill script + schedule. I'll coordinate SLA/monitoring with oncall.
Maya: assigned, will target a PR by EOD Fri. :thumbsup:
Liam: will prototype aggregator changes in staging, aim for Wednesday tests.
Jonathan: mock by Thursday.
Oliver: will run a dry-run of normalization on staging tomorrow, then propose backfill window.
infra-bot: note: scheduled maintenance window 2025-03-05 02:00-04:00 UTC already on calendar — suggest avoiding backfill then.
Sasha: ack, thanks infra-bot.
Maya: one more question — alerting thresholds? p95 > 500ms for cluster, >1s for critical routes?
Sasha: let's start with cluster p95 > 400ms warning, >800ms critical. route-specific thresholds can be added after we see distributions.
Liam: logging/tracing link — aggregator will emit a backfill telemetry event so we can tie spikes to the job.
Jonathan: I'll add a micro-FAQ on the dashboard explaining retention & why some routes may not have historical data.
Sasha: thanks all. I'll send a summary and owner list to #incidents and #eng-oncall so they know the plan. :white_check_mark:
Oliver: thanks — will post back when staging normalization finishes.
Maya: PR: https://git.redwood/company/runtime-http-exporter/pulls/87 (draft)
Sasha: sneaky nit: keep cardinality cap in exporter to 10k per minute per region, enforce via sampler if necessary.
Liam: noted. we'll add a sampler in aggregation if cardinality spikes.
Jonathan: tagging product for visibility: @product (not in thread) — FYI on dashboard changes.
Sasha: closing the thread — follow-ups in PRs and the draft dashboard thread.
